title: Decolonization after the Second World War
summary: When the United Nations was founded in 1945, some 750 million people, nearly a third of the world's population, lived in territories dependent on colonial powers. Between 1945 and 1960, three dozen new states in Asia and Africa achieved autonomy or independence from European rulers. Since the UN's creation, 80 former colonies have gained independence. Fewer than 2 million people now live in the 17 remaining non-self-governing territories.

uncertainty.note: Dated from the end of the Second World War and the founding of the United Nations in 1945; the initial wave peaked between 1945 and 1960, and later anti-colonial transitions culminated with the independence of Namibia in 1990.
